thesis: Triple Flag Precious Metals is a Toronto- and New York-listed precious metals streaming and royalty company. **[Fact]** It provides upfront capital to mine operators in exchange for a percentage of future metal production, earning cash without operating mines or funding mine-level capital spending. **[Fact]** FY2025 revenue was **$388.7 million** (+44% versus prior year); operating cash flow **$312.8 million** (+46%); the portfolio delivered **113,237** gold equivalent ounces (GEOs) against guidance of 105,000 to 115,000 (`investor-documents/sec-edgar/2025-Annual-Report.pdf` MD&A). **[Fact]** At December 31, 2025 the company had **206,531,806** common shares outstanding, an undrawn **$700 million** credit facility (accordion to **$1 billion**), and paid a **$0.23** annual dividend in U.S. dollars.
why_market_wrong: The market may treat Triple Flag as a smaller Franco-Nevada proxy priced for peak commodity cash flows, underweighting the embedded portfolio growth engine. **[Inference]** FY2025 results embed elevated gold and silver prices; if metals normalize, near-term GEO guidance of **95,000 to 105,000** for 2026 sits below the **113,237** GEOs delivered in 2025, so headline growth may stall even as the asset count rises. **[Inference]** Two hundred five development and exploration royalties are not in the 2026 cash-flow path but support management's 2030 outlook of **140,000 to 150,000** GEOs. **[Inference]** The July 2025 Orogen acquisition and February 2026 Northparkes expansion funding commitment add deal-optionality that a pure commodity-beta multiple may not capture.
